label: done
title: Diagnose Disk and GPU terrain edge gaps
details: Reproduced and isolated the Disk/GPU right-edge gap without repository implementation changes. A window-only screenshot loop at /tmp/status-driver-edge-check.sh captures 30 frames and measures the colored terrain endpoint. GPU repeatedly grew a 12-pixel logical blank gap and snapped to zero; CPU control stayed at zero gap. Root cause: MetricHistoryStore applies the high-frequency one-second bucket finalizer to one-second Disk/GPU inputs. Each sparse reading only finalizes the previous reading, so the visible endpoint is one sample behind. TerrainScene advances its camera from the maximum timestamp across all resources at 150 ms cadence with only a one-second delay, exposing up to one second of blank graph before the next sparse sample finalizes. The visible line/fill stop at the final sample while only collision has a hidden right extension. Existing 58/58 checks pass because no test asserts right-edge coverage for one-second committed inputs. Recommended fix: add an explicit committed one-second history path for Disk/GPU that appends each filtered reading immediately, retain bucket averaging for CPU/Memory, keep the visible path truthful and the one-second horizon, and test endpoint coverage just before the next one-second sample. Also share a clock origin and schedule one-second reads against deadlines to remove smaller phase/drift risk. Rejected fixes: a two-second global delay reduces freshness and contradicts labels; drawing the collision extension would fabricate mutable visible terrain; stamping an old sparse sample at a later bucket boundary misstates its time.
